summary: Phase S3's focused suites are green, but correctness review fails the phase because the public transaction orchestrator cannot be composed with either shipped adapter, tenant ownership is only payload-self-consistency rather than database owner validation, real PostgreSQL duplicate races cannot produce the promised replay result, and calibration persistence can mark a zero-volume artifact release-eligible. The shared suite also misses observable adapter differences and the measured branch coverage remains below the track NFR.
blocking_findings: S3-CORRECTNESS-001 [high]: The production orchestration port is disconnected from both persistence adapters. commitMasteryEvidence requires MasteryTransactionalPersistence.transaction plus findCommit/appendReview/compareAndSwap methods (packages/domain/src/mastery/commit-evidence.ts:142-186,264-336), while createDrizzleMasteryPersistence and createInMemoryMasteryPersistence return only MasteryPersistencePort.readSnapshot/commitMasteryEvidence (packages/domain/src/mastery/persistence-ports.ts:33-50; packages/domain/src/mastery/drizzle-mastery-persistence.ts:680-684). No non-test implementation of MasteryTransactionalPersistence exists. The generic orchestration also appends the review before inserting/CASing its referenced card (commit-evidence.ts:293-310), which conflicts with the schema's review-to-card foreign key for a new card, and its StoredMasteryCommit omits student, audit, provenance, and version metadata (commit-evidence.ts:189-207,315-325). The mock-only transaction test therefore proves an API that the shipped database adapter cannot execute. Unify the orchestration and adapter around one typed transaction/command port, persist the complete audited receipt, and add a PGlite orchestration integration test.

S3-CORRECTNESS-002 [high]: Tenant ownership is not enforced against the users table or immutable record identity. Every mastery table independently references schools.id and users.id, but users.id is globally keyed and users.schoolId is not part of any composite foreign key (packages/db/src/schema/users.ts:25-47; packages/db/src/schema/mastery.ts:22-28,77-84,135-142,192-198,238-244,328-334). A payload can therefore claim school A while naming a real student from school B and satisfy every current foreign key. On revision updates, the adapter selects only schoolId/id/revision and then overwrites studentId/objectiveId/variantKey/createdAt (drizzle-mastery-persistence.ts:418-493,534-568), so a caller with a valid revision can retarget an existing card or state to another student/objective inside the school. assertOwnership only compares nested payload fields with each other (drizzle-mastery-persistence.ts:65-99); it never verifies the student's school or the existing row's owner tuple. Add a school-scoped user ownership constraint/check and make CAS predicates preserve the immutable owner/natural-key tuple in both adapters, with adversarial cross-school-user and retarget tests.

S3-CORRECTNESS-003 [high]: Real idempotent concurrency does not implement the promised applied-plus-replayed outcome. The Drizzle adapter performs SELECT-then-write-then-INSERT under serializable isolation (drizzle-mastery-persistence.ts:330-359,647-668), but it neither retries SQLSTATE 40001 nor reloads the winning receipt after a commit unique conflict. portableFailure maps a 23505 to APPEND_ONLY_CONFLICT and every serialization failure to VALIDATION_ERROR (drizzle-mastery-persistence.ts:223-240). The only concurrent-duplicate test uses a double that queues whole transactions before they begin, so the second operation always observes the first receipt and never exercises PostgreSQL snapshot/unique/serialization behavior (packages/domain/src/__tests__/mastery-persistence-transaction.test.ts:69-147,327-346). Add a live PGlite/PostgreSQL race test and implement bounded retry/reload semantics so identical contenders resolve to one applied and one replayed receipt, while stale CAS remains retryable.

S3-CORRECTNESS-004 [high]: Calibration release governance can persist contradictory, unqualified artifacts. The portable calibration command contains only boolean gate claims and omits review/student volume and evaluation metrics (persistence-contracts.ts:124-139), while the Drizzle adapter always stores reviewCount=0 and studentCount=0 but may set all gates and releaseEligible=true (drizzle-mastery-persistence.ts:588-613). Separately, approveMasteryCalibration accepts zero reviews/students, a worse holdout loss, and unrelated approvedBy/audit.actorId, then unconditionally returns approved (commit-evidence.ts:101-120,346-362). This bypasses the v3.2 release-governance evidence that the schema columns are meant to preserve. Carry the mechanical gate evidence through the shared contract, validate the volume/evaluation and approver identity invariants, and test rejection before any transaction.

S3-CORRECTNESS-005 [high]: The in-memory and Drizzle adapters do not cover the same declared input space or observable result. All portable identifiers are bounded arbitrary strings (persistence-contracts.ts:6,30-35,50-55,66-73,88-92,110-114,125-132,151-157,186-205), but the Drizzle primary/foreign IDs are UUID columns (packages/db/src/schema/mastery.ts:22,77,81,135,139,192,238,286,328); contract-valid non-UUID record/idempotency IDs succeed in memory and fail in Drizzle. Even for the shared UUID fixture, in-memory returns commit:<idempotencyKey> while Drizzle returns the bare key (in-memory-mastery-persistence.ts:235-258; drizzle-mastery-persistence.ts:623-646). The shared suite runs the same loose assertions independently and never compares adapter results. Align Zod IDs with storage or use text IDs consistently, and add an exact cross-adapter fixture comparison including valid boundary identifiers.

S3-CORRECTNESS-006 [high]: The committed schema contradicts the Phase S3 strategy's required uniqueness contract. phase-s3-test-strategy.md requires placement uniqueness on (schoolId, studentId, objectiveId, graphRelease, evidenceType) and calibration uniqueness on (schoolId, domain, ageBand, paramsVersion), but both constraints were removed and the schema test was changed to require no unique constraint (packages/db/src/__tests__/mastery-persistence-schema.test.ts:106-129; packages/db/src/schema/mastery.ts:265-279,311-321). The shared CAS fixture forces a new placement and calibration on every card/state revision, revealing an unresolved command-model conflict rather than justifying silent strategy drift. Decide whether these are versioned singleton artifacts or append-only events, then align strategy, command shape, schema, migration, and tests in one direction.

S3-CORRECTNESS-007 [high]: Phase S3 does not meet the track's more-than-80-percent coverage NFR on branches. The focused V8 run reports 90.82% statements, 91% lines, 98.18% functions, but 77.47% branches overall and only 69.49% branches for drizzle-mastery-persistence.ts. Uncovered paths include provider failure mapping and both concurrent CAS loser branches (lines 237,311,487,561), matching the production risks above. Add focused adversarial tests for real transaction conflicts, owner mismatches, malformed persisted JSON, unique natural-key collisions, and incomplete receipts; do not lower the threshold.

test_strategy_violations: The strategy requires a production atomic orchestration path, but transaction behavior is tested only against an incompatible serialized double and no shipped adapter implements its port.
The strategy requires concurrent duplicate and stale-state behavior against the real adapter; the shared PGlite suite contains no concurrent transaction case.
The strategy requires actor/student/school mismatch rejection and cross-school ownership, but tests compare payload school IDs only and never seed a foreign-school user under a claimed local school.
The strategy requires exact placement and calibration natural-key uniqueness, but implementation and schema tests removed both constraints without revising the strategy.
The shared suite does not compare exact observable results between adapters and uses UUID fixtures exclusively despite the portable contract accepting arbitrary bounded identifiers.
Branch coverage is 77.47% overall and 69.49% for the Drizzle adapter, below the track NFR and leaving transaction-conflict branches unproved.
live_contract_violations: MasteryTransactionalPersistence is not implemented by either public persistence adapter, so the exported atomic orchestration has no production execution path.
Mastery rows can reference a student from another school because schoolId and studentId foreign keys are independent.
Identical concurrent Drizzle requests can surface APPEND_ONLY_CONFLICT or VALIDATION_ERROR instead of a replayed winning receipt.
Calibration records can claim volume/evaluation approval and release eligibility while persisting zero reviews and zero students.
Portable identifier validation accepts values that the UUID-backed Drizzle adapter cannot persist, and adapter commit IDs differ for the same request.
prod_wiring_violations: The public root exports both commitMasteryEvidence orchestration and createDrizzleMasteryPersistence, but their required/provided persistence interfaces are incompatible and there is no backend module wiring them together.
The orchestration write order appends review/evidence before the card CAS, which cannot satisfy the shipped review/evidence foreign-key order for a newly created card.
The orchestration receipt drops required audit/provenance/version identity instead of persisting the full immutable commit contract.
retry_recommendation: required: reopen Phase S3 with Red tests for a real orchestration-to-Drizzle transaction, foreign-school user ownership, identity-preserving CAS, live duplicate races, calibration gate evidence, exact cross-adapter parity, strategy-aligned uniqueness, and greater-than-80-percent branch coverage
